DTR · TALK ABOUT A SCENE

A Statue That Watches Itself

STS-HS12-L4-BR300-HSVPAMA1112-BNB-CFI-01 • HS Media Arts 11–12 • Audience Experience, Intention, and Persuasion in Media Artworks
Look at the picture. You will answer some questions about it. Press the play button to hear each question. Record your answer for each question. You can listen to your answer and record it again. Click SUBMIT RECORDINGS when you have answered all the questions.
JUST FOR FUN · OPTIONAL
In 1974, just before his New York gallery show opened, the Korean-born artist Nam June Paik found an empty wall. He placed an old Buddha statue in front of a TV and aimed a live camera at it, so the statue watched itself on the screen. Critics saw an ancient Asian tradition meeting modern Western television, fused into a new art form called video art, and today this class is reporting live from its own version.
Why do you think Paik made the statue, and not the audience, the one watching the screen?
Optional. You do not have to record this one.
